section_summary: This section completes the monograph’s discussion of Japanese commercial, agricultural, political, and allegedly subversive activity in Bolivia, then presents a detailed chapter on Chile and begins another on Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay. It describes Japanese firms, community associations, diplomatic and commercial intelligence collection, propaganda networks, espionage allegations, and collaboration with German or local pro-Axis figures. It also covers Chilean repatriation and relegation measures, Argentine economic organizations, and illustrated maps and organizational charts.

subfiles.title: Japanese Monograph—Latin America: Bolivia, Chile, and Argentina
subfiles.about: Continuation of an intelligence monograph assessing Japanese communities, firms, propaganda, and alleged espionage activities in Bolivia, Chile, and Argentina.
subfiles.summary: The document concludes its account of Japanese commerce, agriculture, community leadership, and wartime controls in Bolivia. Its Chile chapter gives extensive descriptions of Japanese trading companies, cultural and propaganda bodies, strategic mapping, covert correspondence, espionage allegations, repatriation, and relegation. The succeeding chapter surveys the Japanese population and businesses of Argentina and traces Embassy-directed research, propaganda publications, financial institutions, nationalist intermediaries, and suspected intelligence networks. Maps, photographs, and a final organizational chart supplement the narrative.
